title: A criterion cannot name what would discharge it until it is discharged
body:
A criterion cannot name what would discharge it until it IS discharged, because evidence and discharge are the same event.

## The mechanism, from the interface rather than from a census

`intent ac satisfy` is the only verb that takes evidence, and `--evidence <ref>` is REQUIRED on it. There is no verb that attaches evidence to an unsatisfied criterion, and the unsatisfied state shape carries no evidence field to attach it to. So the two things happen in one call or not at all.

The consequence is that a criterion is structurally unable to say, in advance, what would count as satisfying it. The moment it can say so, it has already said it is satisfied.

## Why this is a defect and not a modelling preference: the sibling has the slot

The AT side does not work this way. `intent at green <ST> <AT> --note "<text>"` carries the justification onto the row in the same call, and the note is OPTIONAL rather than a precondition -- so an AT's assertion and its reason land atomically, and a row is never green-and-unexplained.

So the model is inconsistent between its two halves. This is not an oversight about whether evidence matters; the project decided evidence matters and built the slot on one side.

## The cost, measured on a real estate, not predicted here

baize-vc hit this on their port: the coupling destroyed 31 contract fragments, 28 of them unrestorable (ST0024 22, ST0010 6), plus three AT rows truncated inside the test name. That is the cost of evidence having nowhere to live until the moment of discharge -- prose that had a home before the port had none after it, and there was no field to migrate it into.

## What this issue is NOT claiming

It does not claim a number for how many criteria are currently in each state. Any such figure is a property of the moment. Re-drive it with `intent ac list <STID>` per thread and count; do not cite a figure from this issue, because this issue does not carry one.

## Related and NOT the same

The acceptance gate cannot go red from code changing -- `contract.rs:137` resolves a test-backed criterion from stored AT status, and every writer of `AtStatus::Green` is a human verb. That is a separate finding about whether a green means anything. THIS issue is about whether a red can say what it is waiting for. They compound but they are not the same defect, and fixing either leaves the other standing.
